newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Umbono in security firm venture.
newsitem.headline: Umbono in security firm venture.

text.p: Investment company Umbono Investments Ltd said on Wednesday it had formed Bayete Security Holdings with the South African National Civics Organisation and an as yet unnamed trade union.
Umbono would have a 35 percent stake in Bayete and had provided 7.5 million rand in debt financing for a managament buyout, Afzel Patel, Umbono's financial controller told Reuters.

"The investment...is in line with our primary objective of making good long-term investments in companies and promoting fundamental black economic empowerment," Charles Allison, chief executive officer of Umbono said in a statement.
Bayete specialises in industrial security and operates in KwaZulu-Natal, Gauteng, Mpumalanga, Western Cape and North West provinces.
Bayete would be the largest black-owned security company and the fifth largest security firm in the country, Allison said.
Company officials said the union involved in the deal had requested to remain anonymous until the deal had been finalised.
